newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Argentine ADRs stretch recovery.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Argentine ADRs stretch recovery.

text.p: Argentine shares continued to recover Tuesday on stronger volumes as strength in the Dow underpinned most Latin American stocks.
"We're seeing some bargain-hunting," a trader said. "It's just more of a recovery after the recent beating the Argentine market has taken. I think the shares could go higher."
Despite the gains, traders said investors were still worried about the Argentine government's ability to push its austerity package through Congress.
"Nothing has changed on that front. People are still nervous," one trader said.

Argentine blue-chip YPF's American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) firmed two percent, rising 3/8 to 21-1/4 by early afternoon, while Telefonica added 7/8 to 23-3/4 and Banco de Galicia gained 1/2 to 20-7/8.
Most other Latin American ADRs also posted gains, with the Dow's firmness providing support.
Mexico's Telmex up 1/8 at 34, Tribasa rose 1/4 to 4-7/8, and Televisa added 3/8 to 31-1/8.
Brazil's Telebras also rose, gaining two percent, or 1-3/8 to 72-3/4 after falling nearly four percent Monday.
Chilean shares were mixed on low volumes, with blue-chip CTC up 3/8 at 96-3/4, Banco O'Higgins off 1/4 at 22, and Enersis adding 1/8 to 31-1/4.
In other activity, British Petroleum fell about one percent, sliding 1-1/8 to 117-7/8 on heavy volume after Morgan Stanley downgraded the stock to neutral from outperform.
Britain's Hanson gained 1/4 to 12-7/8, boosted by perceived positive comments by its Millenium Chemicals company, which is due to be spun off in an October flotation.
Millenium told Reuters in London it planned a share buyback by the year 2000 after completing debt cutting plans.
"The company is talking about growth and paying back debt, as well as a share buyback. All of these have been taken positively by the market," a trader said.
Among Asian shares, Ek Chor China fell 12 percent, dropping 1-1/8 to 8-3/8. A wire service reported that Ek Chor's first-half profits fell below its expectations.
Shanghai Petrochemical also lost ground, falling one to 26-7/8 after the company reported a 34 percent drop in first-half net to 794 million yuan.
"Shanghai Petrochemical's results were weaker than expected," a trader said.
